findings.title: Success criteria coverage and sequencing
findings.description:
Each criterion in the slice design maps to a task:
- **Criteria 1–2:** Tasks 1.1–1.2.
- **Criteria 3–5:** Tasks 1.3–1.4.
- **Criteria 6–9:** Tasks 2.1–2.3.
- **Criteria 10–11:** Tasks 3.2 and 3.4.
- **Criterion 12:** Tasks 4.1–4.2.
- **Criterion 13:** Tasks 3.5 and 5.1.
- **Criterion 14:** Task 5.2.

Dependencies run in order: enum and config, then enforcement module, then SimulationManager wiring, then YAML defaults. Each implementation task is followed by its tests, and there are no circular dependencies. The slice states no NFR, so no load test or CI-gating task is needed.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkboxes, use the wrong form, and one sits at an untested point
findings.description:
The markers appear as `- [ ] **Commit:** ...` inside separate numbered "Commit" tasks (1.5, 2.4, 3.6, 4.3, 5.5). Markers should be plain `**Commit**:` lines, not checkboxes, and the `git add` steps shouldn't be checkbox items either.

The Section 4 marker (lines 283-286) also sits at an untested point. Tasks 4.1 and 4.2 change `default.yaml` and `test.yaml` to `wrap` and are verified only by a one-line load script. The full suite doesn't run until Task 5.1, after the commit. An existing test that loads a shipped config, or asserts its values, could break on that commit.

Convert the markers to plain lines. Fold the Section 4 YAML edits into Section 3 before Task 3.5, so the regression run covers them and the separate YAML-only commit goes away. Task 5.1 then only repeats Task 3.5 and can be dropped.

findings.title: Test volume exceeds what the success criteria need
findings.description:
This slice is effort 2/5, yet Task 2.3 lists about 17 test functions plus a parametrized one, and Task 1.4 lists 7. Cuts that lose no criterion coverage:
- **Parametrized dispatch test (line 171):** drop it. It only asserts "does not raise", which every per-policy test already proves.
- **`test_open_is_noop_positions` and `_velocities`:** merge them into one test.
- **`test_wrap_single_overshoot_left` and `test_wrap_negative_large_overshoot`:** keep one negative case.
- **`test_reflect_clamps_top_edge` and `_bottom_edge`:** y is the same code path as x, so the diagonal-corner test covers it.
- **`test_bounds_policy_wrap`, `_reflect`, `_case_insensitive` in Task 1.4 (lines 83-85):** merge into one parametrized test.

findings.title: Steps dictate implementation detail the slice does not require
findings.description:
These steps over-specify:
- **Task 2.1:** lists the exact import lines and says to use a `match` statement.
- **Task 2.2:** prescribes `np.mod(..., out=...)` and boolean-mask indexing line by line.
- **Task 1.1:** prescribes alphabetical import placement.
- **Task 1.3:** prescribes `data.get("policy", None)`.

The slice requires only the behavior: in-place, vectorized, correct per policy.

The step in Task 3.2 (line 209) about "zero import-time overhead" conflicts with the Notes bullet (line 329). That bullet says the module-level import is kept and only the call is skipped. The line-329 wording is also garbled ("No import ... is avoided"). Replace the step with a check that matches criterion 10, which is the mock-based test.

findings.title: Several tasks are too granular
findings.description:
These pairs each change a few lines in one file and can be merged:
- Tasks 1.1 and 1.2 (enum plus field).
- Tasks 3.1 and 3.2 (constructor argument plus call site).
- Tasks 4.1 and 4.2 (two YAML lines).

Merging them gives about 3 implementation tasks per section instead of 5–6.

findings.title: Wrap and round-trip tests fall short of criteria 5 and 7
findings.description:
- **Criterion 5:** it requires that reloading the emitted YAML "produces an equal `ServerConfig`". The round-trip test only asserts "policy matches". Assert full `ServerConfig` equality instead.
- **Criterion 7:** it requires every wrapped position to land in `[0, width)`. `np.mod` on a tiny negative float, such as `-1e-20` against 100.0, returns exactly `100.0` because of rounding. That violates the half-open interval. No test in Task 2.3 covers this case, and the implementation steps in Task 2.2 don't address it. Add one tiny-negative-overshoot test, and decide whether to handle the result explicitly.

findings.title: Manual walkthrough steps 5–7 need a human with a viewer
findings.description: Steps 5–7 of Task 5.2 require connecting the Three.js viewer and judging the motion by eye, which a junior AI can't do. Criterion 14 does require this check. Add a `BLOCKED:` line under the task for those steps, as the project convention says for work that needs the Project Manager. Alternatively, run a headless check by stepping `SimulationManager` and asserting positions, as in Task 3.4. Step 8 also leaves `config/test.yaml` edited, so confirm the restore before the Task 5.5 commit.

findings.title: Frontmatter status contradicts the unchecked task list
findings.description: The frontmatter says `status: complete` (as does the slice design) while every checkbox is unchecked. Task 5.3 later sets the same value. Set both files to an in-progress status until Task 5.3 runs, so tooling reading the status isn't misled.

structured_findings.summary: Commit markers are checkboxes, use the wrong form, and one sits at an untested point
Test volume exceeds what the success criteria need
Steps dictate implementation detail the slice does not require
Wrap and round-trip tests fall short of criteria 5 and 7
Manual walkthrough steps 5–7 need a human with a viewer
Frontmatter status contradicts the unchecked task list
